daughter.prompt: a daughter of Eilhaud of Drassone, raised at court

draft.name: Golhine Di Terrou
facts: She stands at five feet and six inches, with a slender frame that has yet to fill out fully, her posture shaped by years of court etiquette drilled into her from childhood.

Her eyes are large and amber-gold with vertically slit pupils, inheriting her mother's Tsevranyan Owl bloodline directly, though her skin is the olive tone of her Drassonais father rather than the plumage.
Her hair is dark brown and thick, falling in loose waves past her shoulders in a style that her attendants struggle to pin into the elaborate arrangements court fashion demands.
Golhine possesses a quick, sharp mind that she masks behind a carefully practiced composure, having learned early that court observers are always watching.
She has inherited her father's dry wit but lacks his patience, sometimes letting a barbed remark slip before she can measure its weight, a habit she is acutely aware of and working to correct.
Beneath her court-trained exterior, Golhine carries a restless curiosity about the world beyond the palace walls, particularly the northern lands of her maternal ancestors.
Born in the autumn of 981, Golhine was raised at the Drassonais court from infancy following the death of her mother, Princess Consort Esrelle, in childbed.
She was educated alongside other noble children at court, though her status as the king's only child set her apart in ways both privileged and isolating.

Her tutors included scholars in Drassonais literature, history, and languages, though she received particular instruction in Tsevrani from a visiting Tsevranyan Owl who recognized her heritage and wished to preserve it.

Golhine's relationship with her father, King Eilhaud, is one of mutual respect tempered by the distance that comes from his absorption in governance and her resentment at being kept from matters of state.
She has no siblings and no close confidantes at court, a fact that has made her both self-reliant and lonely.
She speaks Drassonais fluently with a clipped, precise accent like her father's, but her vocabulary occasionally reveals Tsevrani influences she absorbed from her mother's side of the family.

owl_son.prompt: an owl-folk hunter who watches the stars, a son of Zakan

draft.name: Velesk Zhuskovsk Ul Yechra
facts: Velesk is a tall, lean Snowy Owl with a broad chest and long legs, his white plumage still thick and unblemished at thirty-one, though a faint silvering has begun at the tips of his wing feathers.
His face is sharp and angular, dominated by large, deep-set yellow eyes with dark circular markings that give him an intense, penetrating gaze, inherited directly from his father Zakan.
A narrow, pale scar runs along the outside of his right forearm, a memento from a hunting accident in his late teens that left a thin ridge of raised tissue from elbow to wrist.

Velesk is the second-born son of Tsar Zakan III and was raised in the royal household of Khyagovsk, where he developed a quiet, observant temperament that often went unnoticed amid the noise of court politics.

As a youth, he was more comfortable wandering the forests around the capital than attending to the business of governance, and his early years were marked by a restless curiosity about the wild lands beyond Khyagovsk's walls.

He is an exceptionally skilled tracker and bowman, capable of moving through dense boreal forest without disturbing the snow or leaf litter beneath his talons, a talent he honed through years of solitary hunting expeditions.

Velesk possesses an unusual talent for reading the sky: he can navigate by the stars with a precision that borders on instinct, and he keeps a personal log of celestial observations that he updates every clear night.

He is reserved and deliberate in speech, inheriting his father's clipped Varovni cadence, but where Zakan's silence can be cutting, Velesk's tends toward contemplation—he often pauses before answering, as though weighing each word against the night sky.

Despite his noble birth, Velesk carries himself without pretension and has earned the respect of common hunters and trappers in the northern settlements by treating them as equals rather than subjects.

His relationship with his father is complex: he admires Zakan's strength of mind but resents the weight of dynastic expectation, having made clear from adolescence that he has no interest in court administration or political office.

He maintains a close, affectionate bond with his older brother, who serves as heir to the throne, though their different temperaments—his brother's openness contrasted with his own guardedness—sometimes creates a gentle distance between them.

Velesk speaks Varovni plainly and without ornament, favoring short, declarative sentences. When he quotes the old hunters' sayings of the northern provinces, his pronunciation shifts subtly to a rural dialect that his court-educated companions sometimes struggle to follow.
